lines.name: Berkeley line

operators.name: Key System (the San Francisco, Oakland & San Jose Railway and its successors)

lines.summary: The Key Route's first line, from its pier to downtown Berkeley by Adeline Street and Shattuck Avenue; cut back to Alcatraz Avenue in 1933, then from 1941 over the Southern Pacific's old tracks to Northbrae and, from 1942, through the Northbrae Tunnel to The Alameda.

route.note: Over the Key Route pier to its ferries until January 15, 1939
Over East Bay Transit's tracks to Dwight Way, then the Interurban's
To University Avenue from July 26, 1941; beyond it from August 6, 1941
Ordered by the Railroad Commission on October 27, 1942 (D35900); December 6, 1942 per Demoro

sources.note: Lines named by letter in 1941: "Adeline Street" (F), "Sacramento Street Rail Line \"H\"", "Westbrae Shuttle Rail Line \"G\"".
Train service over the bridge from January 15, 1939.
"The first regular train service over the Key Route was inaugurated on Oct. 26" (1903).

Authority to discontinue the line "along Adeline Street and Shattuck Avenue between the intersection of Adeline Street and Alcatraz Avenue and the end of the line at University Avenue" (March 16, 1933).
To Northbrae Station: "This service was initiated August 6, 1941." Ordered through the Northbrae tunnel to The Alameda "within thirty (30) days from the date hereof" (October 27, 1942).
Through the Northbrae Tunnel to The Alameda from December 6, 1942 (page as Wikipedia gives it).
Authorized "to discontinue transbay rail service and to substitute motor coach service therefor, on its presently existing \"A\", \"B\", \"C\", \"E\" and \"F\" rail lines" (March 12, 1957).
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

lines.notes: Letters were given to the lines in 1939. By 1933 the line ran to University Avenue, not Center Street; when it was extended isn't sourced, and that last stretch isn't drawn. The day of the 1933 cutback isn't sourced. The last trains ran in 1958 (HAER); April 19 or 20, 1958 is given only by later sources.

photo.caption: A four-car Key Route train at its Berkeley terminal, with an Oakland Transit Consolidated car of the Telegraph Avenue line in front and the Southern Pacific's depot at left.
photo.author: Street Railway Journal

"this morning. The event was the reception of the Key route system".
"first opportunity today to use the new extension of the Key System Piedmont electric train … over the present car tracks to Manor station".

lines.name: Key Route ferry

lines.name: Claremont line

operators.name: Key System (the San Francisco, Oakland & San Jose Railway and its successors)

lines.summary: From the Key Route pier, and from 1939 the Bay Bridge, along Yerba Buena Avenue and Adeline Street, then 55th Street and Claremont Avenue to the Claremont Hotel on the Berkeley line.

route.note: Over the Key Route pier to its ferries until January 15, 1939

sources.note: "In 1908 the Claremont line was opened" (a retrospective).
The Fifty-fifth street branch was about to run "from the ferry to Telegraph avenue, on Fifty-fifth street".
"the Fifty-fifth street line, which has already been built as far as Telegraph avenue, will be extended to Claremont avenue and out Claremont to College avenue."

In 1954 the E ran "between the grounds of the Hotel Claremont at Domingo Avenue in the City of Berkeley and the said bridge terminal a distance of 11.14 miles"; its night and Sunday buses ran "closely paralleling the rail routes": "55th Street from Market Street to Vicente Street. … Vicente Street from 55th Street to 56th Street. … 56th Street from Vicente Street to Claremont Avenue. … Claremont Avenue from 56th Street to Russell Street."
Authorized "to discontinue transbay rail service and to substitute motor coach service therefor, on its presently existing \"A\", \"B\", \"C\", \"E\" and \"F\" rail lines" (March 12, 1957).
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

lines.notes: Opened as the Claremont line in 1908 (the Oakland Tribune's retrospective of 1912); before that a branch ran from the ferry to Telegraph Avenue on 55th Street, from 1905 to 1907 (its first day isn't sourced). Night and Sunday service went to buses from November 7, 1954 (CPUC Decision No. 50731). The last trains ran in 1958 (HAER).
